subject: MAP: perf evaluation plan & target close timeline - HealthCore
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Sara Klein <sara@healthcore.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: perf evaluation plan & target close timeline - HealthCore

Sara — attaching the MAP and the evaluation plan we discussed on the call. Key ask: run the baseline perf harness over your representative production traces and return the logs so we can finalize the close timeline. Short summary below, full plan attached (MAP_HealthCore_v1.xlsx + test_script.tar.gz).

Scope / success criteria (short):
- Latency SLO: P95 <= 350ms for user-facing sampling flows (target).
- TTFT (Time-to-first-token): median < 120ms for chat completion in 2k prompt distribution.
- Throughput: sustain 20 concurrent long-running sessions (avg 60 tokens/s each) at <500ms tail latency.
- Concurrency: validate up to 200 concurrent ephemeral inference requests for high-load spikes.

Model variants to evaluate (Redwood catalog):
- rw-7b (fp16) — low-cost low-latency baseline
- rw-13b-v2 (q4/qat) — balanced latency/quality
- rw-70b-int8 — best-quality @ slightly higher latency; aggressive quantized variant
- rw-70b-qat — quantized/optimized 70b variant we propose for canary runs

Evaluation plan highlights:
- Test harness: use the attached test_script.tar.gz with your trace capture; we will run identical harness in our lab for verification.
- Metrics collected: median, p95 latency; TTFT; tokens/sec throughput; GPU utilization; sample-level quality (ROUGE-L on summary set + hallucination check).
- Canary plan: 48h canary with real traffic (5% routed) then progressive ramp to 25% over 72h.
- Decision gates: if p95 > 600ms or TTFT median > 250ms for chosen variant, fallback to rw-13b-v2 + caching.

Proposed timeline:
- 3/22: MAP & harness delivered (this email) — HealthCore runs tests and returns logs by EOD 3/22 PT.
- 3/23: Redwood lab verification + variant analysis.
- 3/24: Joint canary kickoff (if gating thresholds met).
- 3/29: Target production cutover / contract signature.

Attachments: MAP_HealthCore_v1.xlsx, test_script.tar.gz

Thanks — hope this is clear. I can hop on a short 20m call this afternoon if you want to walk through the plan.

—
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP: perf evaluation plan & target close timeline - HealthCore

Mateo — thanks, we ran the first pass this morning using the harness on a subset of our production trace. Attached: healthcore_perf_logs.zip (includes CSVs and aggregated logs). Quick highlights:

- TTFT (median):
  - rw-70b-int8: ~180ms median (we saw a long tail to ~420ms under burst)
  - rw-13b-v2: ~95ms median
  - rw-7b: ~60ms median

- P95 latency (completion end-to-end):
  - rw-70b-int8: 720ms (higher than target)
  - rw-13b-v2: 310ms
  - rw-7b: 210ms

- Throughput: sustained tokens/sec roughly aligned with expectations; rw-70b-int8 showed GPU stalls under concurrent long sequences on our smaller test cluster.

Quality quick check (sample of 200 queries): rw-70b-int8 first-pass had slightly better ROUGE-L (+2-3 pts) on our abstractive set, but we observed a small uptick in hallucination on domain-specific prompts (~1.8% vs 1.2% for rw-13b-v2).

We can run the full harness tonight (will take a few hours) and then send the full artifacts. Given the p95 numbers for rw-70b-int8, we're worried about meeting the P95 SLO without additional infra or aggressive caching. What do you recommend for the canary variant?

—

Forwarding HealthCore's initial perf pass. Sara is seeing p95 >700ms for rw-70b-int8 and a TTFT median ~180ms. She asked what we recommend for the canary variant to meet the P95 SLO without sacrificing too much quality.

Can you do a quick assessment of the logs (attached in the zip) and propose the variant (and config: batching, cache TTLs, quantization knobs) we should propose for the 3/24 canary? Goal: keep p95 <= 350ms while preserving at least ~+2 ROUGE-L vs rw-7b.

Thanks — Mateo
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP perf evaluation plan & target close timeline - HealthCore — assessment

Quick read of the artifacts + local repro. Short recommendation and rationale below — attached is a concise assessment PDF (MAP_Perf_Assessment_20270322.pdf) with the full table and graphs.

Executive recommendation:
- Primary canary: rw-13b-v2 (q4/qat) with prefix caching enabled (cache TTL 30s for session-level prefixes) and batching window tuned to 20ms.
- Fallback: rw-70b-qat for high-quality fallback on specific routes (e.g., discharge summaries) routed by policy (5% of traffic).

Key perf/quality numbers (approx from HealthCore sample & our repro):
- rw-7b (fp16): median TTFT 60ms | p95 210ms | throughput OK | ROUGE-L baseline 42.1 | hallucination 2.3%
- rw-13b-v2 (q4/qat): median TTFT 95ms | p95 310ms | throughput good | ROUGE-L 44.8 | hallucination 1.2%
- rw-70b-int8: median TTFT 180ms | p95 720ms (tail spikes under concurrency) | ROUGE-L 47.1 | hallucination 1.0%
- rw-70b-qat (opt): median TTFT 140ms | p95 380ms | ROUGE-L 46.8 | hallucination 1.1%

Interpretation:
- rw-70b-int8 gives the best single-shot quality but fails the P95 SLO on HealthCore's traces without infra changes. The int8 pipeline in their environment shows KV-cache misses and occasional kernel stalls (we reproduced this on similar GPU).
- rw-13b-v2 balances quality and latency and meets the P95 target when combined with short prefix caching and a slightly aggressive batching window. It achieves ~+2.7 ROUGE-L vs rw-7b at roughly half the tail risk of rw-70b-int8.

Operational suggestions:
- Canary config: rw-13b-v2, batching 20ms, dynamic prefix cache TTL 30s, limit max tokens per request to 1024 for canary, enable token-budgeting to avoid long-run stalls.
- Metrics to watch during canary: TTFT median & p95, p99 tail, GPU mem alloc spikes, request queue depth, hallucination rate on a small probe set (10k synthetic prompts).
- If rw-13b-v2 quality shows regression for specific flows (e.g., medical discharge text), route those flows to rw-70b-qat via routing policy configured in MAP.

Cost note: rw-13b-v2 expected to be ~1.8x rw-7b unit cost; rw-70b-qat ~3.7x. We'll draft a cost/latency tradeoff table for 1M monthly requests if you want to include in the contract addendum.

Attaching: MAP_Perf_Assessment_20270322.pdf (includes plots, tables, and the gating decision checklist). Happy to join the canary kickoff call.

—

Subject: Re: MAP: perf evaluation plan & target close timeline - HealthCore — decision and next steps

Sara / Tom — thanks for the quick turn. Based on HealthCore's logs and Ben's assessment, recommended path forward:

1) Canary variant: rw-13b-v2 (q4/qat) with the operational knobs Ben listed (batching 20ms, prefix cache TTL 30s, token limit 1024). This meets our joint P95 target and preserves the ~+2.5 ROUGE-L improvement over rw-7b on your test set.
2) Selective fallback: route high-value document routes (discharge summaries, legal templates) to rw-70b-qat at 5% traffic initially, monitor quality delta.
3) Verification window: Redwood will run an internal verification of HealthCore's full harness overnight 3/22–3/23 and share the verified report by COB 3/23.
4) Canary kickoff: 3/24 morning — we'll join the kickoff call and monitor the gating metrics in real time.
5) Target production cutover & contract signature: 3/29 pending successful canary.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-final.pdf (final MAP with canary gates & acceptance criteria).

If that works, I'll send a brief canary runbook and calendar invites for the 3/24 kickoff. If you'd prefer rw-70b-qat as primary and want us to size infra to meet p95, we can provide a separate dedicated-capacity estimate (longer lead).

Next steps: Sara — please confirm you want rw-13b-v2 for canary and that HealthCore will provide the full harness artifacts by COB 3/22.
